methodology: An innovative apparatus was designed and constructed to ensure uniform digital imaging conditions for pilling assessment in woven fabrics made from various fibers (cotton, wool, viscose, polyamide6.6, polyester, and acrylic). Pilling was induced using the Martindale pill tester with two different abradant materials through predefined pilling rubs ranging from 125 to 30,000 cycles.
research_objective: To highlight the importance of uniform digital imaging and digital grading in pilling assessment, demonstrating comparability of pilling grades assigned by the standard visual method while providing a distinction between consecutive grades.

key_findings.finding: Uniform digital imaging using innovative apparatus ensures consistency in pilling assessment.
Grading classes based on the total percentage of fabric specimen surface area covered with pills enable objective and consistent grading of fabrics without a reference dataset.
High elongation and work of rupture contribute to good wear resistance.
Natural cellulose fibers like cotton exhibit moderate pilling due to their shorter length and lower strength.
Different imaging devices can prevent comparison of results due to variations in magnification and analyzed surface area.

The software analysis process involves digital image analysis performed by computer programs with different operating methods, including statistical method, shallow neural network method, and deep convolutional network method.
The accuracy of shallow neural network method is lower than that of deep convolutional neural network method.
